newsitem.title: USA: NHL-RECCHI'S HAT TRICK HELPS EAST BEAT WEST ALL-STARS.
newsitem.headline: NHL-RECCHI'S HAT TRICK HELPS EAST BEAT WEST ALL-STARS.

text.p: Mark Recchi of the Montreal Canadiens recorded a hat trick and Mario Lemieux and John LeClair each added two goals and an assist, powering the Eastern Conference to an 11-7 win Saturday over the West in the 47th NHL All-Star Game.
Recchi's hat trick was the eighth in All-Star competition and secured Most Valuable Player honours for Recchi, who had five points in the 1993 game.
"Playing in this game with Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux for the first time was awesome," said Recchi. "Just the way they conduct themselves in the dressing room and prepare was great.
"I was in awe of all the great players in our room and then I win the MVP. Mark Messier set me up twice and Adam Oates and Mario (Lemieux) set up the third goal."

Hometown favourite Owen Nolan of the San Jose Sharks gave Western Conference fans reason to roar when he beat Buffalo's Dominik Hasek on a breakaway with 2:03 remaining for the game's second hat trick.
It was the fourth straight win for the Eastern Conference, which extended its lead in the series to 15-5.
The game provided many special moments as the great Gretzky, a fixture on Western Conference All-Star teams before joining the New York Rangers this season, played for the first time for the East.
Said Lemieux, "This is first time I played with Wayne since the 1987 Canada Cup. He gave me a great pass from behind the net for my first goal."
The East stormed to a 4-0 lead in the first period and never looked back. They struck for two goals on consecutive shots in a 57-second span midway through the period.
LeClair, who plays for the Philadelphia Flyers, redirected a backhanded centering pass from Peter Bondra of the Washington Capitals from the top of the crease at 8:52.

Defenceman Viacheslav Fetisov of the Detroit Red Wings gave the puck away behind his own net and Gretzky set up Lemieux, who put a shot over goaltender Patrick Roy's left arm for his 10th career All-Star goal.
The assist made Gretzky the leading scorer in All-Star history with 20 points. He had been tied with his boyhood idol, Gordie Howe.
The East got two more quick goals late in the period but the West got back in the game as Pavel Bure of the Vancouver Canucks and Paul Kariya of the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim scored a minute apart.
The six-goal first period paled in comparison to the second period, when the squads combined for an All-Star record 10 goals.
Recchi got it started with his second of the game at 1:56 and Geoff Sanderson of the Hartford Whalers put home a backhander 85 seconds later to give the East a 6-2 cushion.

Bure scored his second goal at 4:40, but the Eastern Conference got the next three. Lemieux, likely playing in the final All-Star Game of his illustrious career, beat goaltender Andy Moog on a breakaway at 6:09 and Messier put them ahead 8-3 at 8:45.

Recchi completed his hat trick just over two minutes later and goalie Martin Brodeur of the New Jersey Devils made three spectacular stops from point-blank range to deny Bure's bid for a hat trick of his own.

Paul Coffey of the Philadelphia Flyers picked up a rare All-Star penalty for hooking and the West cashed in on the power play at 16:38 when Brendan Shanahan of the Red Wings beat Brodeur with a wrist shot from the left faceoff circle.
Nolan brought the hometown crowd to its feet and made All-Star history when he scored twice in an eight-second span late in the second period.

His first goal trickled in off his knee off Theoren Fleury's centering pass. After the ensuing faceoff, Nolan put a blast from the right circle over Brodeur's glove. Dennis Ververgaert set the previous record of 10 seconds in 1976.
"The fans here shave been so good to me it made it great just to be here," said Nolan. "When I got the first goal it wasn't enough and the fans increased their intensity.
"That got me going. After the second goal I wanted the third goal more than anything. To hear the fans cheer for me when I got it, is an indescribable feeling."
